title: Fatal Error Recovery
description: Use WordPress recovery mode and safe debugging practices to fix PHP fatal errors without extended downtime.

steps.title: Read the Fatal Error Message
steps.instructions: Check the admin email recovery notice, wp-content/debug.log, or host PHP error log. Note plugin/theme file path, line number, and error type (undefined function, class not found, etc.).

steps.title: Enter Recovery Mode
steps.instructions: Click the recovery mode link in the admin email. This logs you in with the problematic plugin or theme paused. Extend the recovery session if needed.

steps.title: Update or Roll Back Offending Component
steps.instructions: If the error started after an update, roll back the plugin/theme version via backup or vendor changelog. Apply pending updates if the error is from outdated code on new PHP.

steps.title: Check PHP Version Compatibility
steps.instructions: Fatal 'undefined function' errors often mean PHP was upgraded before plugins. Match PHP version to plugin requirements or update plugins for the new PHP.

steps.title: Review Custom Snippets and mu-plugins
steps.instructions: Disable custom code in Code Snippets, functions.php, or mu-plugins that reference removed WordPress APIs. Test after each removal.

steps.title: Validate Fix on Staging First
steps.instructions: Before re-enabling the paused plugin on production, confirm the fix on staging with the same PHP version and active plugin set.

steps.title: Exit Recovery and Monitor
steps.instructions: Re-enable the fixed component, exit recovery mode, and monitor error logs for 24 hours. Document root cause for the client runbook.
